editorial: Get ready for a tense, claustrophobic evening where politeness becomes a weapon. Speak No Evil (2022) sits at the intersection of quiet domesticity and escalating dread, hammering atmosphere into every frame. The standout experience derives from the film’s razor‑thin pacing, turning each pause into an almost tactile dread. You’ll discover that the silence between characters feels louder than the soundtrack, especially during the family rituals. If the film’s subtle use of flashbacks ever feels slow, it simply lets the tension bleed over an extended horizon.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
